direct_answer_summary: Kubernetes v1.31.0 utilizes sigs.k8s.io/yaml v1.4.0 to parse and convert incoming YAML manifests into JSON across the API server, kubectl, and kubelet. It unmarshals YAML into Go structs using standard JSON schema tags, while pinning gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1 for duplicate key rejection.

resolved_tree.role: Kubernetes YAML-to-JSON manifest converter and admission boundary

coexistence.divergence_analysis: Kubernetes 1.31 resolves YAML parsing through a dual-parser architecture. At the admission control and API boundary, sigs.k8s.io/yaml v1.4.0 acts as a strict bridge by transcoding YAML manifests into intermediate JSON representations before schema deserialization. This enforces YAML 1.2 plain-string semantics and neutralizes the Norway problem. Concurrently, gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1 is integrated to provide strict duplicate key rejection, while legacy gopkg.in/yaml.v2 v2.4.0 remains pinned transitively across auxiliary CLI sub-packages, creating subtle parser divergence risks if external CRD operators bypass the standard sigs.k8s.io/yaml pipeline.

parser_hazards.code_good:

parser_hazards.impact: Silent authorization bypass in geographic admission controllers when raw YAML 1.1 unmarshaling is invoked without JSON transcoding.

search_query: What version of OpenSSL is in Node.js 22 LTS?

target.name: OpenSSL
target.role_classification: Canonical Cryptographic Engine & TLS Runtime (node:crypto & TLS 1.3)

other_versions.role: Legacy cryptographic provider for deprecated legacy ciphers (MD4, RC4, Blowfish, DES)
Host operating system dynamic shared crypto library providing ABI collision boundary for native C++ addons

direct_answer_summary: Node.js v22.6.0 embeds OpenSSL 3.0.13+quic as its primary cryptographic runtime engine, providing default TLS 1.3 ciphers, modernized provider architecture, and QUIC packet parsing primitives. Legacy cryptographic algorithms are disabled by default and require explicit legacy provider invocation.

transitory_sbom.provenance_note: No authoritative upstream SBOM published for Node.js v22.6.0. Baseline deterministically synthesized from Google deps.dev dependency graph and verified source tree citations.

resolved_tree.role: Embedded OpenSSL 3.0 cryptographic engine with QUIC API extensions and default provider
Legacy cryptographic provider for deprecated legacy ciphers (MD4, RC4, Blowfish, DES)
Host operating system dynamic shared crypto library providing ABI collision boundary for native C++ addons

coexistence.divergence_analysis: Node.js 22 LTS statically embeds OpenSSL 3.0.13 with specialized QUIC API extensions directly into its core binary (`deps/openssl/openssl`). Unlike prior Node.js LTS releases that utilized OpenSSL 1.1 or monolithic provider setups, Node.js 22 operates under OpenSSL 3.0's modular Provider Architecture. Legacy cryptographic algorithms (MD4, RC4, DES, Blowfish) are isolated into a separate legacy provider (`legacy.so`), causing unhandled `ERR_OSSL_EVP_UNSUPPORTED` runtime exceptions unless `--openssl-legacy-provider` is explicitly enabled. Furthermore, when native C++ npm addons (`node-gyp`) dynamically link against host operating system libraries (`libcrypto.so.3` or legacy OpenSSL 1.1), dual-engine symbol collisions and ABI divergence can trigger fatal segmentation faults during EVP cipher context handoffs.

parser_hazards.title: OpenSSL 3.0 Provider Architecture (Implicit Legacy Cipher Deprecation)
parser_hazards.code_bad:
// Fails with ERR_OSSL_EVP_UNSUPPORTED in Node.js 22:

parser_hazards.code_good:
// Supported in default provider or use modern digest:
const hash = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(data).digest('hex');
parser_hazards.impact: Unhandled runtime exceptions (ERR_OSSL_EVP_UNSUPPORTED) crashing services processing legacy digests or legacy certificates without --openssl-legacy-provider.
